prompt: Some people believe that technology has made communication between people less personal. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?
essay:
In the digital age, technology has fundamentally transformed how humans interact with one another. While some argue that these changes have diminished the personal nature of communication, I partially agree with this view, as technology has both enhanced and hindered personal connections depending on how it is utilized.

On one hand, technology has indeed created barriers to meaningful personal interaction. Face-to-face conversations, which allow for nuanced emotional expression through body language and tone, are increasingly replaced by text messages and emails that lack these crucial non-verbal cues. Moreover, the prevalence of social media has fostered superficial relationships where people maintain hundreds of online "friends" but may struggle to form deep, authentic connections. The phenomenon of individuals sitting together while absorbed in their devices, rather than engaging with those physically present, exemplifies how technology can create emotional distance even in physical proximity.

However, technology has also revolutionized communication in profoundly positive ways. Video calling platforms enable families separated by vast distances to maintain visual contact and share important moments in real-time. Social media and messaging apps have reconnected old friends and allowed people with niche interests to find like-minded communities globally. During the COVID-19 pandemic, technology proved essential for maintaining personal relationships when physical meetings were impossible, demonstrating its capacity to preserve rather than diminish personal connections.

Furthermore, the quality of communication largely depends on individual choices rather than the technology itself. Those who use digital tools mindfullyscheduling regular video calls with loved ones, sharing meaningful content, and setting boundaries on device usagecan maintain deeply personal relationships. Conversely, even traditional face-to-face interactions can be impersonal if participants are disengaged or superficial.

In conclusion, while technology has introduced challenges to personal communication, particularly through the reduction of face-to-face interaction and the rise of superficial online relationships, it has simultaneously created unprecedented opportunities for maintaining and developing personal connections across distances. The key lies not in the technology itself but in how consciously and purposefully we choose to use it.
